hypothesis: Architecture experiment on the label scale. rc5/rc6/rc7 showed the net converges to slope ~1.20 against the reference regardless of data volume (524M vs 1.57B) or learning rate (1e-5 vs 5e-4), so the inflation is a fixed property of the binpack target distribution rather than an optimization artifact: Stockfish 5000-node search scores are roughly 20% larger in scale than the static evals this engine's coordinate system assumes. Raise architecture.json eval_scale 400 -> 480 (400 * 1.20) so sigmoid(search_score/480) lands where sigmoid(static_score/400) did, letting the net learn search-derived rankings while emitting static-eval-compatible magnitudes. eval_scale is a training-time target transform only: it is passed to the trainer as ENYO_BULLET_EVAL_SCALE, is not written into the exported net header, and the engine never reads it, so no engine support is required. Safe with continue_from because resolved_init_weights loads a raw optimiser-state checkpoint directly; the dequantization warning recorded in 7331d1c applies to initialize_from, which alone goes through convert_initialize_from. bullet_output reuses rc5's already-converted corpus so eval_scale is the only difference from rc5.
